searchText: The fact that we are reducing profitability from a similar attack vector that we don't see by more than we are increasing profitability from a new attack vector makes me OK with launching 1559 as-is and considering a separate EIP for addressing the selfish fork choice rule problem. Idea from a discussion thread elsewhere: Have a 1559-like mechanism that targets a certain amount of new state per block and adjusts state write prices up/down based on that. We would then reduce the regular gas cost of state writes to just the "cost of a node to write to disk" and we would not charge regular gas for the "state growth impact". There would be no inclusion fee component to this since it is a socialized cost, not an uncle risk for miners. I don't believe we would need a new transaction type, as the max_fee can already account for this. It would just be an adjustment to the fee deduction algorithm and probably a new field in blocks. We could set the adjustment speed to be really slow if we wanted so seasonality had less of an effect. Was consideration given to initially burning a small portion of the base fee and increasing the percentage over time? It was discussed, but the core devs don't seem to think it will provide any meaningful security benefits. Is it, in any way, detrimental to securtiy? Only if the sudden reward reduction results in a sufficient incentive to attack the network. Then, that would seem like a reasonable way to move the important goals of 1559 forward while treating miners a little less like adversaries and more as valued members of the changing Ethereum ecosystem. With some certainty around the phase-out period, miners can plan operations accordingly and I suspect there would be much less opposition or animosity. This is a better topic for <#798586271445680129>. interesting. i'm generally curious about introducing markets instead of fixed costs where possible There's nothing inherently superior about fixed quantities vs fixed costs; in both cases, one of the two variables is planned and the other is determined by the demand curve what was that phil daian piece about markets for blockchain resources? i guess that would fall under the chicago project and Gastoken In this case, we care about hitting a quantity target, not a cost target.
